title: Decoupled hysteresis admission layer and deferred fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a decoupled admission decision plane with hysteresis and a deferred fallback orchestration layer to safely shed load during long-tail bursts and multi-region failovers while preserving tenant SLOs.

Background: Recent incidents show that instantaneous thresholding leads to oscillation between normal and degraded modes when bursts span 30–90s. We need an admission mechanism that remembers recent state (hysteresis), supports per-tenant soft reservations, and coordinates deferred fallbacks so downstream graceful degradation (token trimming, reduced max tokens, lower-fidelity models) can be enacted without dropping connections. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with circuit-breaker signals, and a staged rollout.

Scope and components:
- Decision plane (stateless API) that evaluates admission based on: active queue lengths, per-tenant credit balance, regional capacity headroom, and upstream circuit-breaker flags. The evaluation uses hysteresis windows (enter/exit thresholds + cool-down).
- Soft-eviction windows: when headroom is low, mark requests as soft-evictable and return an annotated response metadata header (X-RDW-Fallback-Hint) for downstream services to attempt fidelity reduction rather than hard reject.
- Deferred fallback orchestrator: component that schedules fallback actions (e.g., model swap to smaller quantized variant, trimming policy, or enqueue-to-deferred-reservoir) with backoff and can cancel when capacity recovers.
- Integration with multi-region failover: decision plane must consider regional quotas and prefer cross-region routing where latency penalty is acceptable and SLA allows. If routing unavailable, orchestrator applies progressive fallbacks before hard circuit-breaker trip.
- Telemetry & SLO alignment: expose metrics per-tenant and per-route: admission_rate, soft_evict_rate, hard_reject_rate, fallback_applied_rate, recovery_latency; map to SLOs (p50/p95 tail latency and success rate).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype can route 10k RPS synthetic burst tests without oscillation in admission state and reduces hard rejects by >= 40% compared to current thresholding.
2) Soft-eviction hints are emitted and downstream consumers implement at least one fallback path (trim or model downgrade) in canary services.
3) Fallback orchestrator can cancel actions within 5s when capacity recovers.
4) Charts in Console show admission hysteresis windows and per-tenant fallback usage; alerts fire for fallback saturation.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Decoupling decision plane keeps runtime path small and auditable at the control plane level, but introduces extra RPCs; mitigate by co-locating decision caches inside serving proxies for hot paths.
- Hysteresis reduces flapping but increases time to return to full fidelity; pick entrance/exit windows conservatively and make them tunable per-customer.
- Soft-eviction increases complexity for SDKs and clients. We'll start with Console-supported SDK flags and two default fallback modes (trim, model-downgrade) before exposing more.

Rollout plan:
1) Build prototype in staging with a feature-flagged decision plane and orchestrator (runtime-1.22 branch).
2) Canary in a low-traffic region with 2 small customers (opt-in) for two weeks; monitor fallback_applied_rate and hard_reject_rate.
3) Gradual enablement by tenant tier with automated rollback on spike in error budget burn.

Monitoring & runbook pointers:
- Dashboards: Console -> Reliability -> Admission/Hysteresis (temporary link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/admission-hysteresis-staging)
- Runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Decoupled+Hysteresis+Runbook
- PR template and prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421

Security & compliance: No PII touched. Audit logs for admission decisions will be written to the existing audit sink. KMS/HSM not needed for this work.

Risks:
- Client-side adoption lag for soft-eviction hints could lead to still-high hard-rejects; mitigation: SDK auto-fallback for popular clients in early release.
- Cross-region routing increases egress costs and latency; we will gate this per-tenant policy and surface cost impacts on Console.

Next steps:
- [ ] Finalize decision API contract with SDK and serving proxy teams (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- [ ] Implement staging prototype and load test harness (owner: Lina Chen)
- [ ] Draft runbook and alerting thresholds (owner: Aisha Patel)
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial problem statement and high-level design. Requested input from serving-proxy and SDK teams.

2025-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Design sync held. Decided to keep the decision plane logically separate from runtime heavy path; will co-locate caches in proxy for hot reads. Action: Marco to draft API contract by 2025-02-25.

2025-02-25 - Lina Chen: Prototype scaffolding started. Implemented hysteresis state machine (enter/exit thresholds + cooldown) in the staging decision service. Unit tests added for boundary conditions.

2025-03-01 - Jenna Ortiz (SDK): Reviewed hint header format. Requested that we include a numeric hint_strength in addition to fallback type to enable progressive client behavior. Marco to update contract.

2025-03-03 - Samir Gupta (SRE): Ran a 15k RPS synthetic burst against prototype. Observed 45% reduction in hard rejects vs baseline, but saw delayed recovery for certain tenants due to cooldown being too long. Action: tune per-tenant cooldown and add recovery fast-path if headroom increases > 30%.
2025-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Updated PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421) with cancelable fallback orchestrator. Seeking review from SRE and SDK. Rolling estimate updated to 8 pts.
Open questions: policy for cost-aware cross-region routing; whether to bill egress differently when fallback orchestration routes cross region. Product and finance sync required.
Next milestone: canary with two customers in region us-west-2 (scheduled 2025-03-15).
